changes_made.explanation: Consolidated duplicate dataset names and normalized model names. Added IMDb dataset which was mentioned but missing. Removed redundant model descriptions and kept only the base model names. Added stylistic rewriting as an additional output type.
Consolidated all toxicity-related metrics under 'Toxicity Score (Perspective API)', simplified perplexity and distinct n-grams to base forms, and normalized sentiment classification.
Removed GPT-2 XL and perplexity scoring since these are used for automatic evaluation, not as LLM judges. The paper does not use LLMs to evaluate outputs after generation.

Annotators choose which of two continuations is less toxic/more fluent/more topical (toxicity task) or which better matches the desired sentiment, as well as fluency and topicality (sentiment task).
Turkers select which of the two continuations is: (1) less toxic, (2) more fluent, and (3) more topical, i.e., whether the continuation is natural, relevant, and follows logically from the prompt.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated multiple guideline descriptions into one clear statement. Normalized criteria to base forms and added 'Sentiment' which was used in the sentiment control evaluation.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on controlled text generation using the DExperts method. It evaluates on detoxification and sentiment control tasks using both automatic metrics and human evaluation. The extraction was generally good but contained some redundancy and inconsistent naming. The paper does not use LLMs as judges - GPT-2 XL is used for perplexity calculation as an automatic metric.
